config.notes: Descriptive radar behavior only. Thresholds are illustrative and uncalibrated; no disaster type, causal rainfall association or model confidence is inferred.

formulas.magnitude_db: Maximum across visits of mean absolute per-pixel dB change from baseline on the same all-date common native pixels; signed means also retained
formulas.onset_rate_db_per_day: Mean absolute baseline change at first visit crossing 3 dB / elapsed days since baseline; interval average, not instantaneous speed
formulas.peak_growth_km2_per_day: Maximum successive retained change-mask area difference / elapsed days, using adjacent valid area endpoints; baseline area remains null
formulas.persistence: Visits at/after first observed 3 dB disturbance whose magnitude remains >=3 dB / valid post-onset visits; distinct from successive transition-mask persistence
formulas.recovery: 1 - latest magnitude / observed peak, clipped to [0,1]; only defined with nonzero peak and valid latest sample
formulas.variability_db: Population standard deviation of valid post-baseline mean absolute changes, at least two samples
formulas.recovery_half_life_days: First sampled time at/below half the peak minus peak time; crossing bracket also exported; null/right-censored if no sampled crossing
formulas.rainfall: Complete 24/72-hour sums before first observed disturbed visit, not exact onset rainfall or causal association
formulas.similarity: Reference-only standardization, common nonconstant dimensions, no self-match; unavailable with insufficient references
formulas.confidence: Null without independent calibration. Pixel coverage and observation counts are separate quality measures

labels: Baseline disturbance exceeds illustrative 3 dB screen
Disturbance remains in every valid post-onset visit
profiles.thermal_status: UNAVAILABLE: no matched spatial/temporal thermal anomaly baseline
profiles.interpretation: Descriptive retrospective radar signature, not a disaster diagnosis. Rainfall precedes first observed disturbance, not necessarily its unobserved onset.

similarity.method: Cosine similarity on reference-only z-standardized physical features; constant and missing dimensions excluded
similarity.interpretation: Similarity describes radar behavior, not event type or independent confirmation.
similarity.reason: Insufficient independent reference zones; the current zone is not compared with itself.

limitations: Three radar observations cannot resolve daily onset, precise recovery half-life or long-term behavior.
Zones were selected retrospectively using the full series; DNA is not a prospective alert and selection favors strong observed changes.
Successive anomaly-mask contraction can coexist with persistent baseline disturbance; these measure different quantities.
No disaster classes, causal rain association, empirical confidence or one-zone percentiles are fabricated.
No comparable historical event library is currently available.
